item.title: Padrino 0.18.2 release
item.description:
Padrino 0.18.2 is a patch release with fixes for apps in directories Padrino mistook for libraries, the Erubis crash with newer Tilt, --api projects, nested controllers, the generated admin and the generators. To upgrade, change the version in your Gemfile and run bundle update (details below). Thanks to @achiurizo for many of these fixes. One change can affect existing apps (nested controller blocks, below), and generated admin and --api code isn't updated by a gem upgrade, so a few manual edits are listed under "Upgrading".

Changes

  • Nested controllers. After a controller block nested inside another one, routes defined later kept the outer controller's state: later top-level routes got its path prefix, conditions, filters, cache settings, layout and defaults, and its before and after filters ran for every request. Each controller block now restores the options it opened with (#2469).
  • App paths. An app under a directory such as thor-apps/, lib/padrino-blog/ or test/unit/ was taken for library code, so its controller routes answered 404 unless PADRINO_ROOT was set (#2476, @achiurizo).
  • Erubis. require 'padrino-helpers' raised uninitialized constant Tilt::ErubisTemplate when the erubis gem was installed alongside Tilt 2.5 or newer. ERB templates now render with Erubi, or Ruby's ERB when Erubi isn't bundled (#2470).
  • --api projects. New API projects have no sessions, and CSRF protection follows sessions, so JSON POST requests no longer return 403. padrino g app in an API project writes an app that boots (#2472, @achiurizo).
  • Generated admin. Boolean columns in lists show a check mark or a cross instead of an empty cell. A warning flash no longer leaks onto the page after a 404. The layouts no longer load a Google font over plain http or the IE 8 shim (#2478). padrino g admin_page tells a model that fails to load (and shows its error) from one that doesn't exist (#2477).
  • Generators. padrino g in a bundle without padrino-gen says how to add it (#2477). Running padrino g admin or g admin_page again without a terminal keeps edited files and doesn't duplicate Gemfile lines (#2471, @achiurizo). --tiny projects pass their own tests, and g admin in a project without an app/ application exits with a message (#2446, @achiurizo).
  • Smaller fixes. env['sinatra.route'] is set, so APM and error trackers can name Padrino routes (#2473). l(date, format: :short) no longer raises on Ruby 3 (#2474). Mailers without a delivery_method look up sendmail once instead of on every delivery (#2475), all by @achiurizo.
  • Project. Every gem declares Ruby 2.7.8 or later and links to its changelog and source on rubygems.org, and a security policy explains how to report a vulnerability privately (#2468).

Upgrading from 0.18.1

  1. In your Gemfile, change gem 'padrino', '0.18.1' (generated projects pin the exact version) to gem 'padrino', '~> 0.18.2', then run bundle update padrino. If it lists the padrino-* gems instead of padrino (as --api projects do), set each to ~> 0.18.2 and update them by name: bundle update padrino-core padrino-gen.
  2. If you nest controller blocks, check the routes defined after the block that holds a nested one has closed: later in the same file, at app level, and in controller files loaded after it (with three levels, also the routes in the outermost block after the middle one). On 0.18.1 they wrongly got that block's before and after filters, which also ran for every other request of the app, 404s included, and, when defined in the same file, its path prefix, route name and conditions. On 0.18.2 they don't. If a route relied on any of that (its path, its route name in url(...), its conditions, or an access check in a filter), move it inside that controller block or give it its own filter.
  3. If your project was generated with --api and JSON POST requests return 403, delete the set :sessions line from each app.rb, and in config/apps.rb, inside Padrino.configure_apps do, replace set :protect_from_csrf, Padrino.env != :test with set :protect_from_csrf, proc { sessions? && Padrino.env != :test }.
  4. If your project has a generated admin, these edits are optional (under the directory you named with -a, if not admin/):
    • Boolean columns: run yes | bundle exec padrino g admin_page <model> to regenerate a page (this overwrites your edits to it), or in admin/views/<models>/index.* replace each post.published ? tag_icon(:ok) : tag_icon(:remove) with tag_icon(post.published ? :check : :times) + content_tag(:span, post.published.to_s, class: 'sr-only') unless post.published.nil?, with your model and column.
    • Flash after a 404: delete the flash[:warning] = ... line before each halt 404 in admin/controllers/*.rb.
    • Font and IE shim: delete the fonts.googleapis.com link from admin/views/layouts/application.* and error.*, the comment starting <!-- Le HTML5 shim and the [if lt IE 9] block below it from those layouts and admin/views/sessions/new.*, and the font-family: 'Varela', sans-serif; lines from public/admin/stylesheets/application.css.

Nothing else changes: Ruby 2.7.8 or later, Sinatra 4 and Rack 3 are still required.

item.title: Padrino 0.18.1 release
item.description:
Padrino 0.18.1 is a patch release with security fixes for page caching and for generated admin apps, and a fix for the Active Record database tasks. Upgrade with bundle update padrino. Admin apps you generated before need a small manual edit, described below, because generated code isn't updated by a gem upgrade.

Changes

  • Page caching. A cache_key or expires set while handling a request was stored on the route and reused by later requests, so a key built from the request (cache_key "post-#{params[:id]}") could make another visitor receive that request's cached page. A String key and the expiry now belong to the request that set them. A cached page is also now served only after the route's before filters and conditions have run, so access checks written in a controller block or as route conditions apply to cached pages too (#2448).
  • Admin login bypass removed. The sessions controller that padrino g admin generates logged in as the first account when a bypass parameter was sent and the app ran in development, and the login page showed a "Bypass login?" checkbox. An app started without RACK_ENV runs in development, so a deployment that leaves RACK_ENV unset accepted the bypass from anyone. New admin apps no longer have it (#2445; reported by @achiurizo).
  • Mongoid account lookup. The generated Mongoid Account.authenticate matched any part of an email address, so it could pick the wrong account. It now matches the whole address, ignoring case, like the Active Record and Sequel models (#2445).
  • Active Record database tasks. rake db:migrate (ar:migrate), ar:schema:dump and ar:structure:dump create db/ when it is missing, so a new -d activerecord project on Postgres or MySQL can migrate before it has a model (#2433, @achiurizo).

Upgrading from 0.18.0

  1. Run bundle update padrino. If your Gemfile pins 0.18.0, change it to ~> 0.18.1 first. If it lists the padrino-* gems instead of padrino (as --api projects do), set each to ~> 0.18.1 and update them by name: bundle update padrino-core padrino-gen.
  2. If your project has a generated admin, edit two files (under the directory you named with -a, if not admin/):
    • In admin/controllers/sessions.rb, delete the branch that starts with elsif Padrino.env == :development && params[:bypass] and its three lines.
    • In admin/views/sessions/new.*, delete the fieldset that holds the bypass checkbox (check_box_tag :bypass).
  3. If you use page caching (cache: true):
    • A String cache_key set inside a route handler now names only that request's entry, so it no longer produces cache hits. Set it in a before filter instead, or use a block that reads params (cache_key { "post-#{params[:id]}" }). A block runs again for each request, so it must read params or request, not the handler's local variables.
    • A Symbol key (cache_key :my_name) is one entry shared by every request of the route: set it unconditionally, and only on routes whose page is the same for everyone.
    • before filters in a controller block and route conditions now also run when the page comes from the cache.
  4. If your admin uses Mongoid, change the lookup in models/account.rb (or the model you named with -m) to account = where(email: /\A#{Object::Regexp.escape(email)}\z/i).first if email.present?.
  5. Make sure production sets RACK_ENV=production. Running a deployment in development also turns on code reloading and detailed error pages.

Nothing else changes: Ruby 2.7.8 or later, Sinatra 4 and Rack 3 are still required.

item.title: Padrino 0.18.0 release
item.description:
Padrino 0.18.0 is out. It fixes a long list of bugs in the generators and the database rake tasks, makes generated apps safer by default, and adds rake db:dump. It also removes four generator components (the Ohm, MiniRecord and Dynamoid ORMs and Less) whose projects no longer work with current gems, so read the breaking changes below before you upgrade.

Thanks to @achiurizo for his work on this release, and to @ssut, @mistergibson, @Quintasan, @postmodern and @scockram for the reports behind several of these changes. The full list is in CHANGES.rdoc.

Highlights

  • rake db:dump (sq:dump, ar:dump) dumps a Postgres, MySQL or SQLite database to tmp/<env>_dump.sql, or to FILE=. It runs pg_dump, mysqldump or sqlite3, which must be on your PATH.
  • Database tasks that work:
    • rake db:create creates a missing Postgres or MySQL database on Active Record 7.1 and later, instead of reporting it as existing.
    • sq:create and sq:drop no longer need the createdb and mysql command-line clients.
    • The Sequel migrate tasks run in a project with no migrations yet.
  • Safer generated apps:
    • The session cookie is Secure in production.
    • The session secret comes from SESSION_SECRET when it is set.
    • Apps that set Sinatra's host_authorization (Sinatra 4.1 or later) now get that check.
  • Generators:
    • Re-running padrino g component keeps the files you edited.
    • Field modifiers work in any order (email:string:uniq:index).
    • Sequel references fields become indexed foreign keys.
    • Mongoid models get valid field types.
    • Invalid names and options print a message and exit 1, instead of a backtrace.
  • The admin uses Bootstrap 3.4.1 (was 3.1.0), and its erb and slim list pages get the right menu classes.
  • Fixes in the running app:
    • Editing an ActiveSupport::Concern no longer breaks reloading until a restart.
    • Apps mounted under a sub-path serve shared assets.
    • A malformed URL gets a 404 instead of a 500.
    • Sending an email no longer changes how erb templates escape elsewhere in the process.
    • WEBrick shuts down cleanly on TERM.

Breaking changes

  • Removed generator components: the Ohm, MiniRecord and Dynamoid ORMs and the Less stylesheet engine. Projects generated with them no longer work with current gems. 0.18 doesn't change how existing apps run, but padrino g model, g migration, g admin and g admin_page exit with an error in projects that use one of these ORMs.
  • rake ar:create and ar:drop exit non-zero when a database can't be created or dropped, as Rails does. Scripts that ignored those errors now stop there.
  • SqlHelpers.create_db and drop_db take the app's Sequel connection options (create_db(Sequel::Model.db.opts, charset, collation)), if your Rakefile calls them directly.
  • Apps mounted under a sub-path serve files from the shared public/ under their prefix when their own public/<app> doesn't have them. Such a file answers before the app's routes: with public/robots.txt, an app mounted at /blog serves that file for /blog/robots.txt instead of its own get '/robots.txt'.
  • host_authorization: an app that sets set :host_authorization, permitted_hosts: [...] now answers 403 for other hosts. Apps that don't set it are unchanged.
  • Inflections without ActiveSupport: singularize keeps words like status, address and analysis intact. Nested routes with parent: :status use params[:status_id] (was :statu_id).

Upgrading from 0.17

  1. In your Gemfile, set gem 'padrino', '~> 0.18.0', then run bundle update padrino. If your Gemfile lists the padrino-* gems instead of padrino, set each one's version and name them: bundle update padrino-core padrino-helpers ....

  2. If your project uses Ohm, MiniRecord, Dynamoid or Less, switch it first, and answer yes when asked:

    • The ORM: padrino g component --orm=activerecord (MiniRecord models are Active Record models), --orm=sequel or --orm=mongoid.
    • Less: padrino g component --stylesheet=sass (or scss, tailwind).

  3. After switching, remove what the old component left behind:

    • Gemfile: the old gems (mini_record; rack-less, less and therubyracer; Ohm's or Dynamoid's gems). Then run bundle install.
    • Rakefile: PadrinoTasks.use(:minirecord). The switch already added the new ORM's line.
    • MiniRecord: ActiveRecord::Base.auto_upgrade! in config/boot.rb.
    • Leaving Active Record: use ConnectionPoolManagement in each app, and lib/connection_pool_management_middleware.rb.
    • Less: register LessInitializer in app/app.rb, and config/initializers/less.rb.

    Then port your models to the new ORM.

  4. If a script runs rake ar:create or ar:drop and expects it to carry on after an error, handle the non-zero exit.

  5. If an app is mounted under a sub-path, check that no file in the shared public/ has the same path as one of its routes. If no other app needs the file, rename or remove it. Otherwise, give the app a public folder of its own that isn't public/<app>:

    • for example, create blog/public with a .keep file, so git keeps it;
    • move the app's files from public/blog into it;
    • add set :public_folder, File.join(__dir__, 'public') to the app.

    The folder must exist.

  6. If an app sets host_authorization, make sure permitted_hosts lists every host it is served on.

    • The port doesn't matter.
    • Behind a proxy that sends X-Forwarded-Host (or Forwarded: host=), both that host and the Host the proxy sends must be listed, or have the proxy pass the original Host.
    • Rack::Test requests use example.org, so add it in the test environment, or the app's tests get 403.

  7. In projects without ActiveSupport, check nested routes whose parent ends in -s, -ss or -sis, and the url(...) calls that pass its id. Projects that load ActiveSupport, including every project with a generated admin, are unaffected.

  8. Generated files are yours, so existing projects keep their old defaults. To adopt the new ones:

    • Session cookie: change set :sessions, same_site: :lax to set :sessions, same_site: :lax, secure: Padrino.env == :production in every app, including admin/app.rb. The apps share one cookie, and an app without it rewrites the cookie without Secure. Production then sends the cookie only over HTTPS: served over plain HTTP, logins and form posts fail. Behind a proxy that terminates TLS, have it send X-Forwarded-Proto: https.
    • Session secret: in config/apps.rb, use set :session_secret, ENV.fetch('SESSION_SECRET') { '<your current secret>' }. SESSION_SECRET must be 64 characters or more (padrino rake secret prints one). An empty or shorter value makes every request fail with a 500.
    • Admin: to move to Bootstrap 3.4.1, generate an admin in a scratch project and copy public/admin/stylesheets/bootstrap.css, application.css and public/admin/javascripts/bootstrap/* together. Carry over any changes you made to application.css; Font Awesome moved into it. Bootstrap 3.4.1 sanitizes HTML in tooltips and popovers.
    • Smaller fixes in generated files, if they apply to your project:
      • cucumber.yml: use --tags 'not @wip', and drop --strict on cucumber 12.
      • Bacon: add Bacon.summary_on_exit after the boot line in test/test_config.rb, so a failing suite exits non-zero.
      • Sequel on Postgres or MySQL: add test: false to the Sequel.connect calls in config/database.rb, so rake sq:create can create a missing database.
      • Mongoid 9: add Time.zone_default ||= Time.find_zone!('UTC') to config/database.rb.

  9. Run your test suite and boot the app.

Ruby 2.7.8 or later, Sinatra 4 and Rack 3 are still required, as in 0.17.

item.title: Padrino 0.17.0 release
item.description:
Padrino 0.17.0 is out. It runs on Ruby 4.0 and HAML 6 and 7, adds Falcon, Vite and Tailwind CSS to the generators, and fixes a long list of bugs in the generators, the mailer, the reloader and the ActiveRecord rake tasks. It also removes generators for ORMs that are no longer maintained, so read the breaking changes below before you upgrade.

Thanks to @achiurizo, @osbre, @genkami, @matsubara0507 and @Shaisolaris for their work on this release. The full list is in CHANGES.rdoc.

Padrino 0.16.2 is out too. It brings HAML 6 and 7 and Ruby 4.0 to apps that stay on 0.16 for now, such as Middleman sites.

Highlights

  • Ruby 4.0 and HAML 6/7. Padrino also runs with --enable-frozen-string-literal.
  • New generator options: --server=falcon, --script=vite and --stylesheet=tailwind.
  • Faster boot outside development: files are only tracked for reloading in development.
  • Mailers are safe to deliver concurrently, and Padrino's view helpers (link_to, form_for, partial) work in mailer templates.
  • ActiveRecord 7.1 to 8.1 rake tasks work again, and the ActiveRecord model and migration generators take :index and :uniq (email:string:uniq).
  • Generated projects set SameSite=Lax on the session cookie and skip CSRF checks in the test environment.
  • jQuery 3.7.1: --script jquery and padrino g admin copy jQuery 3.7.1 (was 1.9 and 1.11), with an updated UJS adapter.
  • Hardening: static files are served only from the public folder; link_to and form_tag drop javascript: and other unsafe URL schemes; admin access control compares decoded paths.

Breaking changes

  • Removed ORMs. The DataMapper, MongoMapper, CouchRest, Ripple and Mongomatic generators and rake tasks are gone, as are the Compass and ExtCore components. Existing apps keep running, but padrino g model and padrino g migration stop working in projects that use them.
  • -s means --script again. --server no longer has a short alias: use --server=puma.
  • Generators exit with status 1 when they fail, instead of 0.
  • Reloading outside development (enable :reload in staging, for example) needs Padrino::Reloader.enabled = true before Padrino.load!.
  • Admin access control matches string paths as literal prefixes on path boundaries. allow '/posts' covers /posts, /posts/... and /posts.json, but no longer /posts_admin, and regular-expression syntax inside a string is no longer interpreted. A Regexp, such as allow %r{\A/posts/\d+}, still matches as a pattern.
  • Links with other schemes. link_to and form_tag render # for any scheme other than http, https, mailto, tel and ftp, such as sms: or a custom app scheme.
  • CGI. Padrino no longer loads the whole CGI library. On Ruby before 4.0, add require 'cgi' if your app uses CGI::Cookie, CGI.parse or similar.
  • Server auto-detection prefers Falcon over the other servers when neither Thin nor Puma is installed.

Upgrading from 0.16

  1. In your Gemfile, set gem 'padrino', '~> 0.17.0' (or the same version for each padrino-* gem you list), then run bundle update padrino.
  2. If you reload code outside development, add Padrino::Reloader.enabled = true before Padrino.load! in config/boot.rb.
  3. If you use admin access control, check each allow and protect path: list paths such as /posts_admin explicitly, and turn any string that relies on regular-expression syntax into a Regexp.
  4. Write links with custom URL schemes as plain <a href="..."> tags instead of link_to.
  5. On Ruby before 4.0, add require 'cgi' if you use CGI beyond escaping. On Ruby 4.0, add gem 'irb' to your Gemfile to use padrino console, since irb is no longer a default gem there.
  6. In scripts, use --server=NAME instead of -s NAME, and expect a non-zero exit when a generator fails.
  7. Generated files are yours, so existing projects keep their jQuery 1.x. To update, copy js/jquery.js and ujs/jquery.js from padrino-static over public/javascripts/jquery.js and public/javascripts/jquery-ujs.js, and for the admin, copy jquery-3.7.1.min.js into public/admin/javascripts and change the javascript_include_tag line in admin/views/layouts/application and admin/views/sessions/new to it. Re-running padrino g admin also works, but answer n for admin/app.rb and any file you changed: it overwrites them. On custom admin pages, give Bootstrap 3.1's collapse, tab, modal and alert data attributes a data-target instead of a bare href="#".
  8. Run your test suite and boot the app.

Ruby 2.7.8 or later, Sinatra 4 and Rack 3 are still required, as in 0.16.

item.title: Padrino 0.16.2 release
item.description:
Padrino 0.16.2 is a maintenance release for apps that stay on 0.16 for now, such as Middleman sites, which require padrino-helpers below 0.17. It comes out alongside Padrino 0.17.0 and has nothing else from 0.17.

Changes

  • HAML 6 and 7. Block helpers such as link_to ... do, content_for, form_tag and nested layouts no longer fail with undefined method 'block_is_haml?' in HAML 6 and 7 templates (#2317, @achiurizo; reported in #2322 by @kenchan).
  • Ruby 4.0. padrino-core now depends on the ostruct gem, which Ruby 4.0 no longer installs as a default gem; without it, a 0.16.1 app doesn't boot under Bundler on Ruby 4.0. On Ruby 4.0, padrino console also tells you to add gem 'irb' to your Gemfile instead of failing with a LoadError.

Upgrading from 0.16.1

  1. Run bundle update padrino (in a Middleman site, bundle update padrino-helpers). If your Gemfile pins 0.16.1, change it to ~> 0.16.2 first.
  2. On Ruby 4.0, add gem 'irb' to your Gemfile if you use padrino console.
  3. Ruby 4.0 comes with Bundler 4, which removed bundle --binstubs. If Padrino 0.16 asks you to run it, use bundle binstubs --all instead, or run commands with bundle exec padrino. Padrino 0.17 gives the new instruction itself.

Nothing else changes: Ruby 2.7.8 or later, Sinatra 4 and Rack 3 are still required.

item.title: Padrino 0.16.0 release
item.description:
We are pleased to announce the official release of Padrino 0.16.0, the first major release in several years. This release was made possible by the contributions of @achiurizo, @olleolleolle, @crashtech, and many others.

Padrino 0.16.0 primarily modernizes the framework to ensure compatibility with the latest versions of Ruby, Sinatra, and Rack. We've shared more details about this release below.

Changes

  • NEW #2308, #2310 Code modernization. Codebase is now passing Rubocop (11 offenses only) and generator's templates are using modern syntax (@crashtech)
  • FIX #2306 Specs are now passing for Ruby 3.4 (@crashtech)
  • NEW #2306 Added what HTTP Server to use as an option when generating a new project (@crashtech)
  • FIX #2306 Added the HTTP Server to Gemfile as Ruby 3.0 removed WEBrick from the standard library (@crashtech)
  • FIX #2306 Patch Padrino.core by filtering any 'coreext/kernelrequire' (common pattern for gems that override Kernel#require) from caller entries (@crashtech)
  • FIX #2294 Make detect_rack_handler compatible with Rack 3 (@osbre)
  • FIX #2292 Fixes to README and cleanup (@olleolleolle)
  • FIX #2290 Fixes nil error with latest Rack (@nesquena)
  • FIX #2287 Bump to rack ~>3 and add rack to gemspec (@achirizo)
  • FIX #2286 Bump moneta to 1.6 (@achirizo)
  • FIX #2282 Remove FakeWeb, use Webmock (@achiurizo)
  • NEW #2279 Initial Rubocop setup (@achiurizo)
  • FIX #2277 Upgrade deprecations and support Ruby 3.2 (@achiurizo)
  • FIX #2276 Rename MiniTest to Minitest (@kevin-j-m)

New dependencies versions

Padrino v0.16 now requires Ruby >= 2.7.8. This change aligns us with Sinatra ~> 4.0, which we have also changed in this release. Consequently, this upgrade also requires an upgrade to Rack >= 3.0. These updates ensure that Padrino applications are running on secure, modern foundations and can leverage the latest performance improvements and features available from its dependencies.

HTTP Server Configuration

This is the only breaking change in this release.

WEBrick has been removed from the Ruby Standard Library as of Ruby 3.0. This means that applications relying on the default HTTP server will encounter issues when running on Ruby versions 3.0 and above. To upgrade properly, Padrino now requires developers to explicitly specify their preferred HTTP server in the Gemfile. If your application does not have a manual HTTP server defined, add gem 'webrick' to your Gemfile.

When creating a new Padrino application, you can choose a HTTP server with the --server (-s) option. The full set of options are: thin, puma, spider-gazelle, mongrel, trinidad (JRuby), and webrick (default).

Codebase Updates for Ruby 3.4

We have performed a comprehensive refactoring of the codebase. Both the internal Padrino code and the code generated by our scaffolding tools have been updated to align with the syntax and best practices of Ruby 3.4. This ensures a cleaner, more efficient codebase and provides a better developer experience when working with generated files.
